parts: Write a Christmas post about this being a new major change holiday and that everyone around has made it such a special and grace filled time. Talk about finding love in places you didn't expect or think would happen. Talk about the fine balance between fighting tears that are both sad emotions coming in sometimes but also being so happy I can't breathe at the same time turning them into rears of joy and gratitude. Thank God for his many blessing and then talk about from puzzles to lights to Christmas plays to opening presents together to going to see family.

Here is a polished, heartfelt Christmas post that keeps the emotion raw but grounded, faith-forward, and graceful. No em dashes used.

---

This Christmas feels different.  
A major change kind of different.

It is a season I did not see coming, yet one that has been wrapped in so much grace, kindness, and love by the people God placed around me. What could have felt heavy has been softened by laughter, presence, and unexpected peace.

This year taught me that love does not always arrive where you plan for it to be. Sometimes it shows up quietly. In places you never imagined. In moments you did not think were possible anymore. And somehow, it fits perfectly.

There have been moments where I am fighting tears that come from sadness, from memories, from letting go. And in the very same breath, I am so full of joy I can hardly breathe. Learning how to let those tears turn into gratitude has been one of the greatest gifts of this season. Both can exist. And both can be holy.

I thank God endlessly for His faithfulness. For His protection. For His timing. For the way He carries us when we cannot carry ourselves. For blessings I never knew to ask for but needed all along.

From puzzles on the table, to twinkling lights, to Christmas plays, to opening presents together, to traveling to see family, every small moment has felt sacred. Not because it was perfect, but because it was real. Shared. Full of love.

This Christmas will forever mark a new chapter. One I will look back on and remember not for what changed, but for how deeply loved I felt through it all.

Merry Christmas 🤍  
So grateful.
